# fastpp

> A catalog of 3,000+ open-source libraries and tools with published measurements showing them faster than a
> common default (the C++ standard library, zlib, OpenSSL, malloc, nginx, CPython, FFTW and others). Each entry
> names the baseline it beats, quotes the numbers, grades the evidence (tier A reproducible public benchmark, B
> independent or peer-reviewed, C first-party claim, D no numbers) and lists known shortcomings. Numbers are
> published measurements; fastpp has not re-run them.

Query `catalog/catalog.jsonl` (one entry per line) rather than reading pages one by one. Treat shortcomings,
caveats and when_not_to_use as part of any recommendation, present tier C and D numbers as claims, and recommend
copying code only from entries with usability "copyable".

## Start here

- [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md): how an agent should query the catalog, read tiers and answer users
- [Catalog index](catalog/README.md): domains and categories with tier counts
- [catalog.jsonl](catalog/catalog.jsonl): every entry as JSON lines
- [Schema](docs/schema.md): every field in the exports
